site.notes: Two ditches were dug in the 1930's that caused the lake to become more responsive to changes in rainfall (it is primarily a groundwater fed lake). Water clarity is controlled by influx of colored dissolved organic material that is transferred to the lake during wet periods.

site.sitedescription: Sinkhole lake on the Lake Wales Ridge; oligotrophic, monomictic. Located at the Archbold Biological Station. Upland vegetation Southern Ridge Sandhill, slash pine (Pinus elliottii)/wiregrass variant; Sand Pine Scrub, dominated by Pinus clausa, Quercus spp., and Lyonia; Oak Hickory Scrub (Carya floridana, Quercus spp.), and Rosemary Scrub (Ceratiola ericoides). Bayhead vegetation occurs south of the lake.
